part_title: Choosing GenAI Compute and Deploying APIs with AWS App Runner

scenes.title: Compute, containers and customer engagement
scenes.narration: Begin with the GenAI application in the centre and the different types of customer interaction flowing into it: text, voice, and structured data. The slide presents five AWS deployment and engagement options, and the choice depends on what you need to operate. App Runner offers a streamlined managed runtime for a containerized web API. EC2 gives control over the operating system, accelerators, drivers, and runtime dependencies, but leaves patching and instance operations to your team. ECS orchestrates containers using AWS-native task and service abstractions. EKS uses managed Kubernetes for applications that require its ecosystem and extensibility. Finally, Lex and Connect solve a different problem: conversational interfaces and contact-center customer engagement. They can connect to an application running on any of the compute options. Don't compare them solely on scaling or cost; ask what the user experiences and which component owns model inference, orchestration, or human escalation. A simple stateless API may fit App Runner, while self-hosted GPU inference needs a compatible accelerated environment. The architecture decision starts with workload requirements rather than choosing the most complex service.

scenes.title: AWS App Runner
scenes.narration: Trace the deployment path from a source repository or container image to App Runner. The service can build and deploy a supported application source or run a supplied image, then expose a managed HTTPS web service without requiring you to configure an EC2 fleet. The right-hand live URL represents the customer-facing API, while App Runner handles service deployment, health monitoring, and capacity management. The slide highlights scaling and VPC integration options, so distinguish inbound public HTTPS traffic from outbound connections to private databases or services. App Runner is attractive for an API that receives requests, validates them, and invokes Bedrock, provided its runtime and scaling constraints match the design. The application still needs a least-privilege service role to call approved AWS APIs, and sensitive credentials should come from a managed secret rather than embedded source. Also evaluate instance sizing, concurrent request limits, minimum provisioned capacity, and current pricing rather than assuming all idle compute disappears. App Runner simplifies hosting; it doesn't automatically enforce business authorization, prompt safety, or tenant isolation.
